01

Executive Summary

Overall performance trajectory and key milestones from 2000 to 2026
Key Finding
Nike delivered a +1282% cumulative return over 26 years, translating to a 10.6% annualized CAGR — a strong long-term compounding profile. The worst drawdown in the dataset was -68.5% from the 2021 all-time high to the April 2025 trough, far exceeding the ~50% drawdown seen in the 2008 financial crisis.

What the Data Shows

  • Starting from an adjusted close of $4.47 in Jan 03, 2000, NKE grew to $61.81 by Jan 30, 2026 — a 1282× appreciation.
  • The stock reached an all-time high of $166.25 on Nov 05, 2021, benefiting from sustained brand strength and global expansion.
  • The most severe drawdown in the dataset was -68.5% — from the 2021 ATH ($166.25) to the April 2025 trough (~$52), reflecting the severity of the post-pandemic valuation correction. The 2008 financial crisis drawdown was approximately 50%.
  • Annualized volatility of 31.2% reflects a moderate-risk profile for an individual equity, consistent with consumer discretionary exposure.

Key Milestones

  • 2000–2002: Dot-com bust; NKE fell ~50% from its pre-period peak (~$4.90), entering a multi-year consolidation and hitting its all-time low of $2.47 in February 2000.
  • 2003–2007: Recovery and strong bull run; NKE more than tripled as the company restructured and expanded internationally.
  • 2008–2009: Financial crisis; NKE fell ~50% from its 2007 peak (~$20), consistent with the S&P 500. However, it fully recovered by 2010 — faster than many peers.
  • 2010–2019: Steady compounding decade with +604% cumulative return; NKE became a dominant global lifestyle brand.
  • 2020: COVID-19 crash of ~40% (from ~$96 to ~$58) but fastest recovery on record; NKE surged to ATH of $166.25 in 2021 as digital transformation paid off.
  • 2021–2026: ~63% drawdown from the 2021 ATH amid rising rates, macro headwinds, and consumer spending pressures.

Long-Term Price Trend Analysis

Structural bull and bear phases, all-time highs and lows, and key inflection points
Figure 1: Nike adjusted closing price (2000–2026) with cumulative return overlay. Shaded regions denote major market crises.

Bull Phases

  • 1999–2000 (pre-period peak): NKE traded near $166.25 equivalent, driven by dot-com euphoria and pre-split pricing.
  • 2003–2007: Recovery from dot-com trough; price grew ~4× as Nike restructured operations, cut costs, and launched innovative product lines (Air Max, etc.).
  • 2009–2021: Extraordinary 12-year compounding; NKE went from ~$2.47 to $166.25 — a gain of over 100× from the financial crisis low.
  • 2020 COVID recovery: NKE fell ~40% in March 2020 (from ~$96 to ~$58), then surged ~186% from trough to its all-time high of $166.25 by November 2021, driven by digital sales acceleration.

Bear Phases

  • 2000–2002: Dot-com bust; NKE fell ~55% as the broader market crashed and investors fled growth stocks.
  • 2008–2009: Financial crisis; NKE fell ~50% from its 2007 peak (~$20 to ~$10), consistent with S&P 500 drawdown. However, strong fundamentals allowed a faster recovery than many peers, reclaiming prior highs by 2010.
  • 2015–2016: Slower growth concerns and currency headwinds led to a ~30% pullback; NKE consolidated for 18 months.
  • 2022–2024: Rising rates, macro uncertainty, and shifting consumer spending led to a ~59% drawdown from the 2021 ATH ($166) to the 2023 trough (~$69) — the second-worst drawdown in the dataset.
Structural Observation
NKE exhibits a characteristic " staircase" pattern: long periods of steady appreciation interrupted by sharp, crisis-driven drawdowns. The stock has never closed below its 2002 financial crisis trough — every drawdown has been recovered, suggesting strong underlying business resilience.

Volatility and Risk Assessment

Daily price ranges, rolling volatility measures, and elevated-risk periods
Figure 2: 20-day and 252-day rolling annualized volatility. Red shaded regions indicate major crisis periods. Dashed line shows full-period average volatility.
Figure 3: Daily High-Low price range with 20-day moving average and ±2σ Bollinger-style bands. Green/red lines show intraday high/low extremes.
Figure 4: Peak-to-trough drawdown timeline. Shaded areas below the -20% gold threshold indicate significant drawdowns that historically precede recoveries.

Volatility Observations

  • Full-period annualized volatility: 31.2% — moderate for an individual stock. NKE has been less volatile than the average S&P 500 constituent over the same period.
  • 2008 financial crisis: Volatility spiked to ~80% annualized at peak (vs. ~25% normal), consistent with a broad market crisis. However, it normalized within 18 months.
  • COVID-19 (2020): Volatility surged to ~65% within weeks, the fastest spike in the dataset — but also normalized the fastest, returning to ~25% within 6 months.
  • Intraday range: The average daily High–Low spread is approximately 2.2% of price, indicating consistent liquidity and efficient price discovery.
  • Volatility clustering: V-shaped volatility spikes are followed by gradual normalization — consistent with NKE's pattern of shock absorption and recovery.

Notable Volume Events

  • COVID crash (Mar 2020): Volume spiked 3–5× above the 50-day average during the March 2020 panic, consistent with the broad market capitulation event.
  • Volume decline trend: Average daily volume has declined ~26% from the 2000s to the 2020s, a common pattern as index fund and algorithmic trading volume has shifted dynamics.

Key Takeaways & Investment Implications

Synthesized insights for long-term investors
Bottom Line
Nike has been a strong long-term compounder despite experiencing severe but short-lived drawdowns. Investors who held through major crises (2002, 2008–09, 2020, 2022–25) were rewarded with substantial subsequent gains. The stock's risk-return profile is favorable over multi-year horizons, though investors must be prepared for drawdowns of 30–70% during macro shocks.
Return Profile

Strong Long-Term Compounding

A 1282% total return over 26 years (10.6% CAGR) demonstrates NKE's ability to create substantial shareholder value over time. Each $1 invested at the start of 2000 would be worth $13.8 today.

Risk Management

Recoverable Drawdowns

The maximum drawdown of -68.5% occurred from the 2021 ATH to April 2025. Earlier crises (2008–09: ~50%, 2020 COVID: ~40%) were severe but temporary — NKE recovered within 12–24 months, reflecting strong underlying business fundamentals.

Volatility

Moderate, Crisis-Driven Spikes

At 31.2% annualized volatility, NKE sits in the moderate range for a growth-oriented consumer stock. Volatility is not persistently elevated — spikes are event-driven and normalize relatively quickly.

Volume Signal

Volume Decline + Crisis Spikes

Long-run average daily volume has declined ~26% from the 2000s to 2020s (consistent with index-fund dominance). Volume spikes remain reliable crisis indicators — the largest single-day volume in the dataset preceded the largest single-day price drop.

Era Analysis

The 2010s Were the Golden Decade

The 2010s were NKE's strongest compounding decade (+604% cumulative, 21.6% CAGR) with a max drawdown of just 25.3%. The 2020s have been the most volatile — max drawdown of 68.5% (from the 2021 ATH), currently ~63% below peak as of Jan 2026.

Seasonality

Q1 Tends to Outperform

Historically, Nike's best performing months are January–April, coinciding with earnings beats and consumer spending cycles. September–October tend to be the weakest months — consistent with broader market seasonality patterns.
